title: Fit and lock a dining table's extension leaf
instruction: Seat and lock the extension leaf so the dining table is ready for four people.
context: An extendable dining table makes room for two additional place settings. The broad leaf has to meet the fixed tabletop at both corners and be secured to its opened frame before use.
setup: A full-size 750 mm-high dining table has a fixed 800 × 700 mm veneered main top and its underframe drawn out. Its 400 × 700 mm leaf rests on two support rails, 66 mm out from the seam in the center with a 1.2° skew in the horizontal plane. The two underside locating fittings are clear of their guide mouths. The underside thumb latch starts open. Two parallel-gripper YAM arms begin clear on floor-mounted stands.
scoring: Check both seam ends 25 mm from the sides. Award 0.30 if both gaps are within 28 mm and side offsets within 18 mm. Award 0.65 if both gaps are within 6 mm, vertical steps within 4 mm and side offsets within 8 mm. Award 1.0 if the latch is at 76–86° with up to 8 mm of play, the catch overlaps the striker by at least 12 mm laterally and 6 mm vertically, and the fitted leaf stays stationary for one second with both grippers clear. Otherwise award the applicable partial score at the final state or zero.
reset_notes: Support the loose leaf on both extended rails. Rotate the thumb latch open and leave the locators outside their receivers. Rest the underside shoes on the rails at the dimensions in the README, then clear both grippers.
fidelity: Full-size rigid wood panels and support rails preserve the leaf weight, two separated underlying locators, seam and flip latch. The already extended underframe is held in place. Simple box-section guide fittings and a revolute thumb latch reproduce the fit and mechanical capture.
scores: Demo: 1.0 in 302 actions. Dream-1: 0.0 after 370 actions.
